_readme: Every user-facing string in the web app. Edit ar.json (or copy it to a dialect) against THIS file: en.json is the source of truth and its key set is enforced at build time and by strings.spec.ts. Placeholders in {braces} are substituted at render time and must survive translation exactly.

participant.noVisits: You have no visits assigned right now.

consent.title: Before you start
consent.collectedBody: Your device's location, sampled while this page is open and in front of you, from the moment you start the visit until you end it. Nothing is collected before you start or after you end.
consent.usedBody: To judge how well the evidence supports the visit having happened. It produces a score and a list of reasons — never a simple yes or no, and never proof that you were somewhere. A human reviews anything uncertain.
consent.keptBody: The raw location trail is deleted automatically after the retention window, by the database itself rather than by a job someone has to remember to run. The summary of the visit is kept. A photo you attach is kept with the report, not deleted on that schedule.
consent.cannotBody: It cannot follow you in the background. If you lock your phone or switch apps, it stops receiving your location, and the gap is recorded as a gap. You can end the visit at any time.
consent.readPrompt: Please read the four sections above before agreeing.
consent.versionNote: Consent version {version}. Your agreement is recorded with a server timestamp.

ready.advice: Start the visit as you arrive, and keep this page open and in front of you while you are inside. Your phone can go back in your pocket between interactions — the gaps are expected.

visit.permDenied: Location permission is off, so nothing is being recorded. Turn it on in your browser settings — without it this visit cannot be verified.
visit.permUnsupported: This browser does not provide location. Try Chrome or Safari.
visit.backgroundNotice: This page is in the background, so your location is not being recorded right now. That is normal and the gap is expected — bring the page back when you can.
visit.offlineNotice: You are offline. Fixes are being saved on your phone and will send themselves when you reconnect.
visit.screenAwake: screen kept awake while this page is open
visit.waitingFirstFix: Waiting for a first fix. This can take a few seconds outdoors and longer inside.
visit.endingNotice: Ending the visit stops location capture. You will write your report next.

discreet.explain: Dims the screen to a plain clock so the page is not obviously open. The visit keeps running and location keeps recording.

report.title: Your report
report.notesHint: Greeting time, staff helpfulness, queue length, cleanliness…
report.submitted: Report submitted. It is being reviewed — you do not need to do anything else.

ended.neverStarted: This visit was never started, and was closed automatically after {mins} minutes.
ended.wentQuiet: No location update arrived for {mins} minutes, so this visit was closed automatically. Capture stops when the screen locks or the tab is backgrounded.
ended.noReport: This visit was ended but no report was filed within {mins} minutes, so it was closed automatically.
ended.expired: This visit reached the {hours}-hour limit for a single session and was closed automatically. Location was no longer being recorded.
ended.generic: This visit has ended and can no longer be continued.

evidence.attachHint: Optional. One photo of the shopfront, receipt or display — up to 6 MB.
evidence.tooLarge: That photo is too large. Maximum 6 MB.
evidence.wrongType: Only JPEG, PNG or WebP images can be attached.

history.title: My visits
history.empty: Nothing here yet. Assigned visits and their results will appear here.
history.noFeedback: No written feedback was left on this visit.
history.autoApproved: Approved automatically. Nobody needed to review it.
history.reviewedByPerson: Reviewed by a person at the business.
history.pendingExplain: Your report is with the business. You will be told here when they decide.
history.countedOver: Totals cover your {count} most recent visits.

presence.checkingHint: Your first location reading is on its way. This takes up to half a minute.
presence.insideHint: Stay on site and keep this page open until you are done.
presence.near: You are close to {venue}, but not inside it
presence.nearHint: Move closer, or further in. Right now this would not count as a visit at the venue.
presence.outside: You do not seem to be at {venue}
presence.outsideHint: Check you are at the right branch. Nothing is wrong yet — the visit is still open and this will change as soon as you arrive.
presence.unknown: Your location is not accurate enough to tell
presence.unknownHint: This is normal indoors and is not counted against you. Near a window or a door usually helps.

console.title: Visit console
console.disclaimer: Verdicts describe how much the evidence supports a visit. They are not proof of presence — see the reasons on each visit.

table.empty: No visits yet. Completed visits appear here on their own.

review.title: Override
review.explain: A decision here is recorded alongside the engine's verdict, never instead of it.
review.feedbackHint: The participant reads this. Your reason above stays internal.

dashboard.title: Overview
dashboard.noData: No completed visits in this window yet.
dashboard.trendHint: Each bar is one day. Height is the number of visits that ended that day.
dashboard.failuresHint: Which checks cost visits the most, across this window. This is where to look first.
dashboard.noFailures: No failing signals in this window.

people.title: People
people.subtitle: Results per participant over the last 30 days, worst pass rate first.
people.notCheating: This ranks who needs looking at, not who is dishonest. A run of rejections is equally consistent with a participant inventing visits, a venue saved at the wrong coordinate, or a phone with poor indoor GPS. The 'top issue' column is what tells those apart.
people.empty: No completed visits in this window yet.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.subtitleAdmin: Create business accounts, and the people who sign into them.
accounts.subtitleBusiness: The people in your organisation who can be assigned visits.
accounts.passwordNotice: Every account created here uses the password demo1234. There is no email in this build and no password reset — tell the person their username and that password.
accounts.newBusinessHint: Creates the organisation and its first sign-in together. An organisation with nobody in it cannot be logged into.
accounts.orgSlugHint: Becomes the organisation id: {id}. It cannot be changed later.
accounts.orgRequiredHint: An admin has no organisation, so a new user needs one naming here.
accounts.name: Name
accounts.usernameHint: Lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes. It becomes the account id and cannot be changed.
accounts.deactivateHint: Deactivate: they can no longer sign in. Their past visits are kept.
accounts.reactivateHint: Reactivate: they can sign in again.
accounts.businessCreated: {name} created. They can sign in now with the password above.
accounts.userCreated: {name} created. They can sign in now with the password above.

venueForm.explain: The geofence radius is per venue, never a global constant — a kiosk and a hypermarket cannot share one. 25 to 500 m.
venueForm.name: Name
venueForm.coordinatesHelp: Right-click the spot in Google Maps and paste
venueForm.coordinatesLink: That is a share link, not a coordinate. Open it, right-click the pin, and copy the two numbers.
venueForm.coordinatesCoarse: Only {count} decimal places — that locates the venue to within hundreds of metres. Use at least 4.
venueForm.clientOrgIdHelp: Admins have no organisation of their own, so this is required
venueForm.indoorExplain: Indoor venues legitimately report far worse accuracy, and the engine is told not to punish it.
venueForm.created: Venue "{name}" created with a {radius} m geofence.
venueForm.updated: "{name}" corrected to {lat}, {lng} with a {radius} m geofence. Visits already started keep the geofence they began with.
venueForm.mapHint: Drag the map to put the pin on the venue.
venueForm.searchPlaceholder: Search for a place or address
venueForm.searchFailed: Address search is unavailable right now — drag the map instead.

venueList.title: Venues
venueList.explain: Correcting a venue is safe: a visit that has already started is judged against the geofence it began with, so a fix here never changes a verdict already reached.
venueList.name: Name

taskForm.explain: A task belongs to the venue it is defined against, and inherits its organisation from it.
taskForm.title: Title
taskForm.briefHelp: What the participant should actually do. They read this before starting.

assignForm.explain: This opens a pending visit for that participant straight away. The same participant cannot be given the same task twice.
assignForm.assigned: Assigned to {who}. Their visit is now waiting in the participant app.
assignForm.dialogBody: {who} now has a pending visit at {venue}. It is waiting in their app and they have been notified.
assignForm.noParticipants: No participants in that organisation yet — create one on the Accounts tab.

taskList.title: Tasks
taskList.empty: No tasks yet. Create a venue, then a task against it.

verdict.explainAuto: The evidence is consistent with a real visit. This is not proof of presence.
verdict.explainReview: The evidence is ambiguous. A human decides.
verdict.explainRejected: The evidence does not support this visit having taken place as described.
